html:
A port city on the Mediterranean at the western edge of the Nile Delta, founded by Alexander the Great in 331 BCE. It was laid out on a grid between the sea and a lake, and it served as the capital of Egypt for nearly a thousand years.

After Alexander died, his general Ptolemy made it the capital of Ptolemaic Egypt. It became the largest city of the Greek world, famous for the Lighthouse on the island of Pharos and for the Library, where scholars such as Euclid worked. Greeks, Egyptians and a large Jewish community lived side by side; the Hebrew Bible was translated into Greek there.

Cleopatra was its last Ptolemaic ruler. Under Rome it was the second city of the empire, and its harbour shipped the grain that fed Rome. It was a leading centre of early Christianity and of late Greek philosophy until the murder of Hypatia in 415. After the Arab conquest of 641 the capital moved inland to Fustat, later Cairo, and Alexandria slowly declined.
